newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber up on buying, INRO shrugged off.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber up on buying, INRO shrugged off.

text.p: The Singapore rubber market finished up due to shortcovering on Friday with the trade convinced the International Natural Rubber Organisation (INRO) will not immediately intervene in the market, dealers said.

The rubber business had been waiting for the possible intervention of INRO after the five-day indicator priced ended on July 10 at 182.48 Malaysia/Singapore cents a kg, below the 183.00 cent level where INRO 'may-buy' to support rubber prices. "After the announcement by INRO, prices even went up. It's not necessary for them to come in. Maybe they'll come in at the must-buy level" of 172.00 cents, a dealer said.
With most of the trade not expecting INRO to intervene, buyers engaged in mild shortcovering in the local market.
"Iran made some inquiries. China was also asking for some quotes," one dealer said.
Dealers said the covering was mostly for TSR20 rubber as buyers tried to secure several hundred tonnes of material in the afternoon session.
At around 0445 GMT, September RSS3 was seen at 93.50 U.S. cents a kg from 91.50 cents. August RSS1 was seen at 131.00 Singapore cents (91 U.S. cents) a kg from 128.50 cents.
